author.name: Efficiency Emilia
author.role: Uses deep domain knowledge to define business goals, objectives, and KPIs. Aligns ML features with overarching product strategy and organizational roadmaps. Evaluates system performance, operational capability, and project costs.

challenge.name: The Cost Cliff
challenge.description: The infrastructure bill for the monitoring stack has doubled, and #efficiency_emilia# has drawn a hard line: she will not fund automated drift monitoring, insisting it is a luxury the business cannot afford. #reliability_ruth# argues that without automated and governed drift checks, the team is flying blind during promotion weeks, and she refuses to accept a manual process as a substitute for reliable signal.

output.content: I am flagging the manual scheduling gap between drift alerts and model retraining. When an alert fires, a human must currently log in, verify the signal, and manually queue the retraining job. This adds unnecessary latency and operational overhead to our weekly cycle. I want this hand over to be fully automated. The retraining trigger should fire immediately upon a confirmed alert, removing the need for manual intervention. More automation here is better. It reduces the risk of delayed response and frees up engineering hours for higher value work. I am not asking for a partial fix. I want the entire path from detection to retraining to run without a human in the loop. This is a priority for the next sprint.
output.reclassify_reason: The author explicitly states that 'more automation here is better' and emphasizes the desire for full automation to reduce risk and free up engineering hours, indicating that exceeding the minimum requirement would increase their satisfaction.
